basis: Gestational trophoblastic tumor of the reproductive system, which has no axis; metastatic sites are not defining organs.
PTCRA-related combined immunodeficiency; bronchiectasis in 2/2 supports pulmonary damage. Anemia and other findings lack established direct attribution.
Isolated sperm flagellar dysfunction and male infertility; reproductive function has no axis, and endocrine dysfunction is not demonstrated.
Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation disorder with defining developmental impairment and epileptic encephalopathy; optic disc hypoplasia is very rare.
Cutaneous mastocytosis with clonal mast-cell proliferation in skin; telangiectases do not establish a separate vascular disorder.
Occlusion of retinal venous circulation defines both an ocular disorder and a vascular occlusive disease.
Disorder of the nasopharynx, included in the upper respiratory airways; infection is not shared across this umbrella.
Malignant tumor arising in the exocrine pancreas; neuroendocrine differentiation does not establish endocrine dysfunction. Jaundice is occasional.
Hearing and ear malformations plus renal malformations define the syndrome; renal hypoplasia/aplasia is frequent. Other organ defects are occasional.
Embolic obstruction of pulmonary arteries is vascular disease; pulmonary infarction occurs in a minority and is not required.
Isolated congenital atresia of a bronchus directly affects the lower respiratory airway.
Sexual dysfunction of the male reproductive system; vascular, neurologic and endocrine causes are not universal defining features.
GnRH deficiency and olfactory developmental defects define ANOS1-related Kallmann syndrome; unilateral renal agenesis occurs in approximately 30%.
Tumor originates in the fallopian tube, a reproductive organ outside the axes; abdominal symptoms do not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Nonsyndromic intellectual disability with developmental delay and microcephaly; no established systemic metabolic phenotype is supplied.
Inherited cardiac electrical disorder with shortened QT interval and arrhythmias; syncope does not establish neurologic damage.
GPI biosynthesis disorder with developmental impairment and cerebellar atrophy; osteopenia in 8/8 and myopia in 30-79% support bone and ocular involvement.
Iris hypoplasia and hereditary glaucoma directly affect the eye; the neurological ancestor does not establish extraocular nervous-system disease.
Mature B-cell lymphoma arising in the lung; pulmonary origin, hematologic cell lineage and lymphoma mechanism all apply.
DMD-related isolated dilated cardiomyopathy; muscle histology and gene identity alone do not establish common skeletal muscle functional damage.
UV-induced skin damage; neurodegeneration affects roughly half of XP-D patients and ocular surface damage exceeds 30%; hearing damage frequency is uncertain.
Vibrio infection of the intestine; dehydration and electrolyte changes are acute consequences. Acute kidney injury is occasional (5-29%).
Partial 18q duplication commonly causes developmental and intellectual impairment; other malformations vary with the duplicated segment and lack reliable frequencies.
Multiple joint dislocations and respiratory insufficiency from tracheomalacia or lung hypoplasia define the syndrome; brain abnormalities occur only in some.
Hereditary prostate cancer affects a reproductive organ outside the axes; urinary obstruction or skeletal metastases are not defining features.
